## Intent
Hypothesis: scalar per-particle processing with branchy respawn and no intermediate storage cannot approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout packs 68 B/particle, but loop 1 touches only 32 bytes (47% hot) and loop 2 touches 28 (41% hot), so over half each cache line is dead weight. The death verdict stays in registers, forcing branchy respawn inline. The scalar approach processes one particle per 68-byte stride with no vectorization, compounding the low hot fraction — every line brings data the loop never reads. The working set spills L1d at N≈481 and L2 at N≈7710, but since the loop is instruction-bound these transitions should matter less than for a streaming kernel.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p curve is flat across all N: at q=0.01 it ranges 25.4–26.7 ns/p from N=10000 to N=10M. The L3→DRAM transition (knee at N≈246723) adds only ~0.9 ns/p (25.8→26.7). There is no cache-spill knee because the algo is frontend-stalled at 64–70% across every regime — never bandwidth-limited. Cost is dominated by instruction fetch/decode of a long scalar body, not data movement; the dense grid would not resolve a knee.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 1.95–2.68 GB/s — 15–21% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; actual cost is 25–35 ns/p, 5–6.5× the floor, confirming the algo is far from memory-bound. It is frontend-bound (65–70% frontend stalls, 0% backend, 0% branch_flush). The winner is 1.8–3.3× faster; the gap narrows with death rate — 3.3× at q=0.01 but 1.8× at q=0.5 — because the autovec winner's advantage erodes when branchy respawn dominates, yet even at q=0.5 the scalar code is still 1.8× slower.

## Assembly
The codegen is entirely scalar: 0 vector-suffixed instructions. Loop 1 uses `vmovss` for stride-0x44 loads/stores, `vmulss`/`vaddss` for integration, `vucomiss`+`jae` for the death check, `rorx`/`lzcnt` for the PRNG, and a `call` to spawn — a long branchy body explaining the 65–70% frontend stalls. Loop 2 renders with `movzx` byte loads, `cmp`/`cmovae` 0xff clamping, and `mov BYTE PTR` byte-granular stores — a scatter that cannot stream. A `div` for respawn-index modulo further serializes.

## Verdict
Refuted — this is the baseline (1.0× at every point) and 1.8–3.3× slower than the winner everywhere: 3.3× at q=0.01/N=10000, still 1.8× at q=0.5/N=1000000. The mechanism is frontend starvation (65–70% stalls) from a long scalar loop body with zero vectorization, byte-granular render scatter, and branchy respawn — sustaining only 15–21% of the streaming ceiling and 5–6.5× over the memory floor regardless of cache regime or death rate.
